name: Conway the Machine
sources: style-research-extended vol.1 boom-bap — Conway the Machine
Ambrosia for Heads — Daringer & Beat Butcha on producing without samples (https://ambrosiaforheads.com/2019/12/griselda-daringer-beat-butcha-no-samples-wwcd/)
notes: The same label as Westside Gunn and the opposite drum sound, which is the whole reason this is a separate model: "dry, hard kick 1 and 3.5, snare 2&4… heavy transient, no room tone". So where his labelmate's accents top at 102, these reach 127, the mains sit at 86–100, and `humanize` is the tightest in the batch — `quantizeStrength` 0.9, `velocityVar` 0.1, `timingJitterMs` at 1–2 ms across the kit. "No room tone" is a placed hit with nothing around it, and that is what those three numbers say. The other research fact is that some of these records contain no samples at all: "the harmony is *played* (Rhodes, Moog, strings) but written to imitate a dusty loop". `chords.impliedByRiff` is therefore true even though a player made it — the loop-imitating behaviour, not the source, is what the flag describes — and `i–iv` is authored at weight 3 because the research names it as the one motion that occurs. ⚠ The `i–VII` family at weight 1 is **INFERRED**; the research names static `i` and occasional `i–iv` only. ⚠ `hihat.continuous` is false at `fillDensity` 0.32 for "hats sparse or absent", which is the emptiest a declared hat block may legally be. ⚠ `confidence` is medium: the research rates it medium-high because the producers documented the construction *method* — no samples, played parts — which is not the same as documenting a velocity or a density. Every number in `drums` here is that inference. ⚠ The bass ceiling came down from 41 to 39 so it stays under a chord part that starts at 40 — `coherence.rs` requires the highest bass note to sit at or below the lowest chord note, and this model overlapped by 2. ⚠ **The 1-bar phrase length was removed** (was [1,2], now [2,4]). A one-bar phrase looped four times carries less entropy than a four-bar phrase, and it is the countermelody it strangles hardest: a counter answers *inside* the melody’s phrase, so a one-bar shape leaves it nowhere to go. Every worst offender on `counter.rs` carried it. ⛔ The previous session recorded this exact mistake and it arrived again from the other direction — distinctness is combinatorial in the shape LENGTH, not in the option count.
